name: Claude Code Session Storage Model
description: Claude Code's local session-persistence design: append-only JSONL files, one per session, stored under ~/.claude/projects/<path-encoded>/<session-uuid>.jsonl, where each line is a typed event chained via parentUuid into an event stream. Storage is project-path-scoped on disk and complemented by a dual instruction/memory layer (hierarchical CLAUDE.md files + Auto-memory under the per-project memory/ directory). The most documented real-world session-persistence design; maps cleanly to a MongoDB event-document model.

identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Device-local with no per-session account binding at the storage layer. Claude Code is a local CLI; session transcripts, CLAUDE.md, and auto-memory live on the developer's machine under ~/.claude/ and are implicitly owned by the OS user. Authentication is to the Anthropic backend for model access (Claude.ai OAuth login or an Anthropic API key / cloud-provider credential), but the session-storage model itself carries no user identity field — files are scoped by filesystem path and project, not by an account ID. There is no anonymous-vs-required distinction for storage; whoever has filesystem access to ~/.claude/ owns the sessions.
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: Not a collaboration/multi-user storage model. Sessions are single-user, local, and per-machine; there is no shared-workspace, team, or org-isolation concept at the session-storage layer. Sharing happens indirectly: a project-root CLAUDE.md is committed to version control and thus shared with the whole team via git, while transcripts and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md / auto-memory are personal and not checked in. Managed (enterprise) policy CLAUDE.md files can be installed system-wide and cannot be excluded, which is the closest thing to org-level control, but that governs instructions, not session sharing. [uncertain]

workspace_model.workspace_definition: A workspace is a filesystem directory (typically a git repo working directory / cwd). Claude Code derives a project key by URL/path-encoding the absolute project path into a single directory name under ~/.claude/projects/ — e.g. /Users/you/code/my-app becomes the folder -Users-you-code-my-app. All sessions started while cwd is inside that path are stored under that encoded folder, so the workspace maps 1:1 to an on-disk path. It is not an abstract cloud entity; the path IS the workspace identifier. This guarantees session data from different projects never mixes and can be inspected or deleted per-project.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Sessions are bound to the project (encoded path) on disk, and each session is a distinct <uuid>.jsonl file inside that project folder. A user can have many sessions per workspace (each prior conversation is its own file) and can run multiple sessions concurrently (e.g. parallel terminals or git worktrees, each producing its own session file). Resumption is path-sensitive: --resume/--continue look up sessions relative to the current directory, so resuming from a different cwd will not find the file. A global ~/.claude/history.jsonl indexes sessionId-to-project entries across all workspaces.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Three nested scopes. Session-level: the JSONL transcript (running conversation, tool calls, results, thinking, token usage, model, cwd, gitBranch per event). Workspace/project-level: project-root CLAUDE.md, nested-directory CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/*.md, and the per-project Auto-memory directory ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/MEMORY.md. Global/user-level: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/settings, applied across every project. Tool/MCP configuration and settings cascade similarly (enterprise/system, project .claude/, user ~/.claude/).
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: Hierarchical CLAUDE.md cascade, auto-loaded at session start by walking from cwd. Levels: (1) Enterprise/managed policy (e.g. /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md) — cannot be excluded; (2) Project memory (project-root CLAUDE.md, committed to VCS); (3) Module memory (nested-directory CLAUDE.md, e.g. src/api/CLAUDE.md); (4) User/global memory (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md); plus Local memory (.claude/CLAUDE.md, not checked in) and .claude/rules/*.md (same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md; rules support a 'paths' frontmatter glob to scope to matching files). Precedence: managed > project > user, with more-specific (deeper-directory) memory overriding broader memory. @path imports are supported (relative or absolute, e.g. @docs/api.md, @~/.claude/file.md), recursive to a max depth of 5, text files only, with a first-time-import approval prompt; imports are ignored inside code blocks. Anthropic recommends keeping CLAUDE.md under ~200 lines.
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Not a bounded-source-corpus / RAG-notebook product. Grounding is the live filesystem of the working directory plus the auto-loaded CLAUDE.md hierarchy and auto-memory; Claude reads files on demand via tools rather than from a curated, pre-ingested source set. There is no NotebookLM/Perplexity-Space-style notebook of fixed PDF/web/video sources scoping retrieval — the 'corpus' is whatever is reachable on disk under the project path. [uncertain]

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Local files, append-only. Each session is a JSONL file (one JSON object per line) at ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-path>/<session-uuid>.jsonl; a global ~/.claude/history.jsonl indexes sessions. Writes are append-only and immediate — every message/event is flushed to disk as it is generated, nothing is rewritten or deleted, giving crash resistance (at most the last unfinished line is lost) and avoiding locking/corruption of prior data. CLAUDE.md files are plain markdown on disk; auto-memory is markdown under the per-project memory/ directory. Via the Agent SDK, a pluggable SessionStore adapter (append + load methods, plus optional methods) can mirror transcripts to external backends (S3, Redis, a database) so a session created on one host can be resumed on another.
persistence_and_history.session_history: Append-only JSONL event stream per session. Each line is a self-contained, typed event with a top-level 'type' discriminator (user, assistant, system) and fields including uuid, parentUuid, timestamp, sessionId, cwd, gitBranch, version, plus message.content (text/tool_use/tool_result/thinking content blocks) and message.usage. parentUuid chains events into a linked list, capturing the full causal order of user turns, assistant responses, tool calls with exact inputs/outputs, extended-thinking blocks, sub-agent spawn events, per-turn token usage, model selection, and git-state snapshots. Sub-agents get their own <uuid>.jsonl plus a .meta.json (agent type + assigned task); the main session keeps only a marker that a sub-agent was invoked. History is browsable/resumable via the CLI (claude --resume shows a picker; -r <id> resumes a specific session; -c/--continue resumes the most recent). Files are plain JSONL and fully exportable/portable by copying them. Known bug: with --input-format stream-json, prior history can be duplicated per turn; consumers should dedupe by message id/uuid.
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Explicit dual (really tri-) layer. (1) Ephemeral session state = the JSONL transcript / running token context for one conversation. (2) Durable user-authored instructions = the CLAUDE.md hierarchy (enterprise/project/module/user/local) — human-written, version-controllable, deterministic. (3) Durable auto-generated memory = Auto-memory: Claude decides on its own what is worth persisting across sessions (build commands, debugging insights, architecture notes, code-style preferences, workflow habits) and writes it to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/MEMORY.md (and topic-specific files alongside). Auto-memory requires Claude Code v2.1.59+, is on by default, and can be forced on/off via CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY (0 = force on, 1 = force off). This cleanly separates short-term thread state (JSONL) from long-term cross-session knowledge (CLAUDE.md + auto-memory), and within long-term separates user-authored from machine-authored.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: No built-in semantic/full-text search index over past transcripts; retrieval is file-based and path-scoped. The CLI's --resume picker lists recent sessions for the current project, and ~/.claude/history.jsonl can be queried with shell tools (jq) to find prior sessionIds by project/cwd. Cross-session continuity of knowledge (rather than verbatim transcript search) is achieved through the persistent CLAUDE.md + Auto-memory layer, which is auto-loaded into every new session so prior context carries forward without manual copy-paste. Because files are plain JSONL on disk, third-party tools/MCP servers can index or grep them, but that is external to the core model. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Persistent by default with no built-in TTL or automatic expiration — session JSONL files, CLAUDE.md, and auto-memory remain on disk until the user (or external tooling) deletes them. Per-project folders under ~/.claude/projects/ allow targeted cleanup by removing a project's directory. There is no archive-vs-hard-delete distinction at the storage layer; deletion is a filesystem operation. Sessions are not discarded at session end (unlike ephemeral cloud-agent models) — the whole point is durable, resumable, append-only history. Retention is therefore an external/operational concern (manual deletion or a user's own cleanup script).

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: In-process / direct on the developer's machine by default — Claude Code operates on the real working directory with the user's filesystem and shell, not an isolated VM/container. Isolation between concurrent sessions is achieved by separate cwds, separate terminals, or git worktrees (each yielding its own session file). The session-storage model itself is filesystem isolation by project path. For sandboxed execution, Claude Code can be run inside an external sandbox/VM (e.g. e2b, CI containers), where transcripts live inside that environment; this is a deployment choice layered on top, not an intrinsic part of the storage model. Network and resource limits depend on the host environment, not the storage design. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: No native filesystem/environment snapshotting independent of conversation history. What persists is the conversation (JSONL), instructions (CLAUDE.md), and auto-memory — not installed packages, env vars, or a restorable machine image. Resuming a session restores conversation context only; the surrounding filesystem/env is whatever currently exists on disk. git state is recorded per event (gitBranch, git snapshots in the transcript) for traceability, but that is metadata, not a restorable environment snapshot. Environment reproducibility is delegated to git + the user's own tooling.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Local-first, but cross-host/cloud handoff is supported via the Agent SDK SessionStore adapter: by mirroring the append-only transcript to shared storage (S3/Redis/DB), a session started on one machine (or in a serverless/cloud sandbox) can be resumed on another, since the model is just a portable JSONL stream keyed by sessionId. Without such mirroring, resume is bound to the local file on the originating machine and cwd. Self-hosting the storage is inherent (it is your filesystem). [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: Supports parallelism and sub-agent fan-out at the storage level. Multiple top-level sessions run concurrently (separate terminals / git worktrees), each its own session file. Sub-agents spawned within a session each get their own <uuid>.jsonl plus a .meta.json describing the sub-agent type and assigned task; the parent session stores only a reference event noting the sub-agent invocation, keeping the parent transcript compact while preserving full sub-agent context in separate files. Sessions can also be forked (--fork): the fork copies history up to the branch point, gets a new sessionId, and diverges independently while the original is unchanged — mirroring an event-log branch.
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Primarily the Claude Code CLI: interactive TUI, plus headless/non-interactive mode (claude -p) for automation in CI/CD, pre-commit hooks, and build scripts. The Agent SDK (Python/TypeScript) exposes query() with continue/resume/fork options to initiate or extend sessions programmatically. Sessions can also be launched inside sandboxes (e2b) or other automation contexts. For CI, the recommended pattern is to capture session_id from --output-format json and resume with --resume <id> rather than relying on --continue (which has no prior session in a clean clone).

implementation.implementation_stack: Local filesystem persistence using JSONL (newline-delimited JSON) as the event format — append-only, one file per session, no database engine required for the core model. Directory convention: ~/.claude/projects/<url-encoded-absolute-path>/<session-uuid>.jsonl, with a global ~/.claude/history.jsonl session index. Event records are typed (type discriminator) and parentUuid-chained, carrying message content blocks, usage, timestamps, sessionId, cwd, gitBranch, and version. Instruction layer is plain markdown (CLAUDE.md hierarchy + .claude/rules/*.md with @path imports, depth<=5); auto-memory is markdown under per-project memory/. Optional pluggable SessionStore adapter (append/load) enables mirroring to external backends (S3, Redis, generic DB). Backend model access authenticates via Anthropic OAuth/API key but is orthogonal to the storage format. Auto-memory gated by env var CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY and version (>=2.1.59).
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: Very high applicability — this is the cleanest blueprint for Labmate's session model. The append-only, parentUuid-chained JSONL event stream maps almost directly onto a MongoDB event-document collection: one document per event, fields { _id/uuid, parentUuid, sessionId/thread_id, type, role, content, usage, ts, gitBranch?, cwd? }, with an index on (sessionId, ts) and a parentUuid pointer to reconstruct the causal chain — giving the same crash-safe, immutable, easily-replayable log without rewriting prior state. The project-path-encoded folder generalizes to a workspace_id field on every event (Labmate would scope by workspace_id rather than a filesystem path), and the global history.jsonl maps to a lightweight 'sessions' index collection in Mongo (one doc per session: { sessionId, workspace_id, user_id, created_at, updated_at, last_event_ts }). For the active/hot path, mirror the most recent events into Redis Streams keyed by sessionId (XADD per event, with TTL) — analogous to Claude Code's immediate-flush behavior and the SDK's SessionStore-to-Redis option — and persist the durable record to Mongo, matching Labmate's existing Mongo+Redis+LangGraph stack (the LangGraph thread_id = Labmate sessionId = Claude Code sessionId). Adopt the dual memory layer explicitly: (a) user-authored durable instructions as a per-workspace 'instructions' document (the CLAUDE.md analogue, with an enterprise>project>user precedence rule encoded in code), and (b) agent-authored Auto-memory as a separate per-workspace memory collection the agent writes summaries into across sessions, kept distinct from raw transcript. Use the Discord connector identity as user_id (the layer Claude Code lacks, since it is device-local) and scope all retrieval by (workspace_id, user_id). Borrow sub-agent storage (separate session docs + a parent reference event) and fork semantics (copy events up to a branch checkpoint, new sessionId) directly. For history retrieval, replicate Claude Code's path-scoped resume as a Mongo query by (workspace_id, sessionId) and surface a 'resume/picker' endpoint; add full-text/vector search on top (which Claude Code lacks) if cross-session transcript search is needed. Caveat for Labmate: unlike Claude Code, build TTL/retention in deliberately (Redis hot tier expires; Mongo cold tier retained with an explicit policy), since the file model has no built-in expiration.
